name: Doximity Scribe vs Freed
title: Doximity Scribe vs Freed: AI Medical Scribe Comparison
description: Compare Doximity Scribe and Freed AI scribes for clinicians. See differences in pricing, EHR integration, features, and which is better for your practice.

summary.bottom_line: Doximity Scribe is completely free for verified US clinicians but requires copy-paste to EHRs. Freed costs $39-119/month but offers EHR push integration and ICD-10 coding suggestions on Premier. Choose Doximity Scribe for free documentation with manual EHR entry; choose Freed for native EHR integration and coding assistance.

sections.heading: Doximity Scribe vs Freed: Overview
sections.content: Doximity Scribe and Freed are both AI-powered medical documentation tools that listen to patient visits and generate clinical notes. Doximity Scribe is free for all verified US clinicians on the Doximity network (85%+ of US physicians), making it the most accessible option for those who qualify. Freed is a paid service ($39-119/month) that offers more advanced features including native EHR integration and ICD-10 coding suggestions. The key trade-off is cost vs. integration depth.

sections.heading: Pricing Comparison
sections.content: Doximity Scribe is completely free for individual clinicians with a verified Doximity account (US physicians, NPs, PAs, medical students). There is no paid tier for individuals. Freed offers three plans: Starter ($39/mo, 40 notes), Core ($79/mo, unlimited notes), and Premier ($119/mo, EHR push + ICD-10 codes). For clinicians who qualify for Doximity, it's unbeatable on price. For those wanting advanced features or who don't qualify, Freed offers significant value at its price points.

sections.heading: Feature Differences
sections.content: The key difference is EHR integration: Freed Premier offers native EHR push to systems like Athenahealth, SimplePractice, and Elation, while Doximity Scribe requires copy-paste. Freed also provides ICD-10 code suggestions, patient instructions, and referral letters on Premier. Doximity Scribe integrates with Doximity Ask (formerly DoxGPT) for note refinement and has the advantage of zero audio storage. Both support in-person and telehealth visits with customizable templates.

sections.heading: Which Should You Choose?
sections.content: Choose based on your budget and integration needs:

recommendations.when: You're a US-verified clinician, comfortable with copy-paste workflow, want zero cost, or already use Doximity for networking and communication
You need native EHR integration, want ICD-10 coding suggestions, are outside the US (not eligible for Doximity), or prefer a dedicated AI scribe platform
You qualify for Doximity—try it free, then evaluate if paid Freed features justify the cost for your workflow

faqs.a: Yes, Doximity Scribe is completely free for US physicians, nurse practitioners, physician assistants, and medical students with verified Doximity accounts. There is no paid tier for individuals. Enterprise licensing is quoted separately for health systems.

faqs.q: Can international clinicians use Doximity Scribe?
faqs.a: No, Doximity Scribe requires US verification. International clinicians should consider Freed or other AI scribes like Nabla that don't have US-only restrictions.

faqs.q: Does Freed integrate with more EHRs than Doximity Scribe?
faqs.a: Freed has deeper EHR integration with native push capabilities to select EHRs (Athenahealth, SimplePractice, Practice Fusion, Elation, Tebra) on Premier. Doximity Scribe works with any EHR but only via copy-paste.

Both report high accuracy (Freed claims 95%+). Doximity Scribe intelligently filters casual conversation from clinical content. Real-world accuracy depends on specialty, accent, and clinical context. Try both if eligible.
